prompt: What did the officer say the stop was based on? Select all that apply.

options.label: A traffic violation (e.g. speeding, no turn signal)
Bad driving that isn't a violation (e.g. weaving within the lane)
A vehicle problem (e.g. equipment, expired registration)
A vehicle or person the officer recognized (e.g. an owner with a suspended license)
Your client matched a suspect's description
Your client ran from or avoided the officer
The officer saw what looked like a crime (e.g. a drug deal)

_author_notes: REVIEW CAREFULLY: which of these reasons suggest a no-reasonable-suspicion issue is decided in the trigger of no-reasonable-suspicion-for-stop and no-reasonable-suspicion-for-pedestrian-stop. Those thresholds haven't been legally reviewed yet; see the REVIEW CAREFULLY note in each issue. The options themselves (and whether to add or cut any) are also worth a second look.

prompt: Did the traffic violation or vehicle problem the officer described actually happen?
Did the caller give their name or other identifying information?
Before the stop, did police see anything themselves that confirmed the tip?
Did the officer know anything suggesting the person they stopped wasn't the person they had in mind (e.g. the driver didn't match the registered owner's description)?
How detailed was the description your client matched?

options.label: Specific: clothing, a particular vehicle, a plate number, or other distinguishing details
General only: race, sex, age range, or similar
